items.title: Harness v2 Week-One Wedge
forge init: per-file collision check for non-empty targets
Briefed, bounded, measured delegation boundary
items.story: As a developer running Claude and Codex together, I want the handoff to be briefed, bounded and measured so that a run cannot stall silently, finish half the job, or ignore the rules I already wrote down.
acceptance_criteria: stage done refuses an empty diff, an out-of-scope change, a missing required test, or a failing per-task verify command
task stages are strictly sequential inside one story worktree, and task-level --parallel is refused
a decomposition recording prose where a runnable command belongs is refused
a --write delegation with no fresh recorded brief is denied by the hook, and the refusal names the command that fixes it
the generated brief carries the acceptance criteria, the write scope with its existing modules, and inlined design rules for user-facing work
forge codex status reports the write flag per job and flags a stalled one
forge doctor reports a required skill a runtime cannot load
forge next names the delegation step
items.outcome: Developers can now see the epic-to-story dependency hierarchy, start dependency-ready stories in separate worktrees, and execute each story's tasks sequentially through a protected, measured delegation boundary that refuses off-contract writes, overlapping workers, stale proof, and incomplete verification.

items.title: Legacy repo upgrade: one command, no residue
items.story: As an orchestrator upgrading a client repo vendored before the factory/ rename, I want one command to carry it onto the current harness, so that no stale copy of the gate surface survives and no story that was open at upgrade time becomes unclosable.
acceptance_criteria: Upgrading a repo that carries .agents/ leaves no .agents/ tree and a complete factory/ tree
Skill-evolution state (proposed, rejected) and client-added skills under .agents/skills/ survive at factory/skills/
A path under .agents/ with no counterpart in the vendored factory/ tree aborts the upgrade and is named; nothing under it is deleted
The upgrade output names every project-owned file still referencing .agents/, excluding archived evidence under .factory/history/
The migration modifies no project-owned file
Upgrading a repo already on factory/ behaves exactly as before
forge stage migrate --base <sha> records that base for each legacy stage it adopts, and refuses a base that does not resolve or is not an ancestor of HEAD
items.outcome: A repo vendored before the factory/ rename can now be carried onto the current harness in one command. `forge upgrade` detects the legacy .agents/ layout, carries the project's skills across, deletes the old tree only once every file left in it is provably the machinery being replaced, and otherwise refuses before writing anything — so a refusal leaves a clean repo you can repair and re-run. It then names the project-owned files still mentioning the retired path instead of editing them. `forge stage migrate --base <sha>` gives a story that was open at upgrade time a measurement origin, so it can still be closed. Four client repos were stranded with no migration path; decision 0016 promised them one and this is it.

items.title: The planning lock guards the harness's own source
items.story: As a maintainer dogfooding this harness on itself, I want the planning lock to treat factory/, docs/, constitution/ and harness/ as product IN THIS REPO so that a change to the gate machinery goes through a plan or a bounded window, the way every client's product code already does.
acceptance_criteria: A write under factory/ in the harness's own repo is refused without an approved plan with a recorded decomposition, or an open quickfix window.
The same paths stay writable during planning in a client repo, where they are vendored harness surface rather than the client's product.
A quickfix window in the harness repo claims the files it touches against its five-file budget, so the closed ledger entry reports the real scope instead of zero.
A test proves the two repo kinds are classified differently, so the distinction cannot silently regress.
items.outcome: The planning lock now guards the harness's own machinery in its own repo: a hand-edit to factory/, constitution/, harness/, .claude/ or .codex/ here needs an approved plan or a bounded quickfix, exactly as a client's product code does — while a client repo's vendored copy of that machinery stays freely writable during planning. Repo kind is a positive .factory/harness-source.json sentinel (never vendored), and a quickfix pins it at start so deleting the marker mid-window can't unlock machinery. A harness-repo quickfix now claims the machinery files it touches against its five-file budget instead of reporting zero.

items.title: Project and spec capture is complete or refused
items.story: As a developer opening a project I have not seen, I want the brief and its capability specs to be guaranteed complete, so that the board can show me what this product is instead of rendering blanks.
acceptance_criteria: record_signoff.py refuses when docs/product/BRIEF.md is missing a required heading or a required heading's body is empty, and names the heading.
forge spec confirm refuses a spec without an H1 title, Why, Behaviour, or Acceptance criteria, and names what is missing.
forge spec save still accepts an incomplete draft.
The brief template, its conventions doc and docs/product/BRIEF.md carry one canonical heading set including Target Outcome, and no heading in an already-written brief is renamed.
A brief or spec captured before this contract is reported by forge doctor and refused by nothing that already passed.
items.outcome: A brief or spec that is missing a required section is now refused at the gate that records it, instead of reaching sign-off half-written. Sign-off names every absent BRIEF heading, spec confirm requires Why, Behaviour and Acceptance criteria, and doctor reports legacy documents without blocking anyone. One shared parser answers 'does this document have this section' for all three, and it reads an example as an example: headings inside fenced blocks, HTML comments, raw blocks and container blocks no longer count as structure.

items.title: The roadmap hierarchy contract
items.story: As a planner, I want epics and stories to be refused unless they carry the fields the hierarchy needs, so that what the board draws is guaranteed to exist rather than hoped for.
acceptance_criteria: roadmap derive, import and add refuse an epic missing id, title, objective or resolvable source_refs, and a story missing narrative, acceptance criteria, skill, a known epic, or an explicit depends_on.
forge roadmap epic add creates an epic after sign-off, proven against a roadmap that has none.
The roadmap add --no-spec ad-hoc path still works and plan save still refuses to build its output.
mark_status, assign, link-spec and heal all still succeed against a roadmap captured before this contract.
unblocks, leverage and epic gating are derived from depends_on, and no route accepts them as authored input.
items.outcome: A story on the roadmap now has to say what it is: the three routes that author stories refuse one that omits its epic, narrative, acceptance criteria, skill or an explicit depends_on. Two new commands make that requirement satisfiable after sign-off — roadmap epic add creates an epic, set-epic points an existing story at one — and this repo's own roadmap was backfilled through them, so forge roadmap list finally prints its epic above the stories. Legacy roadmaps still load, still flip status and still heal; doctor reports their gaps without blocking, and no longer crashes on the broken state it exists to diagnose.

items.title: Plan and task contract
items.story: As a reviewer six weeks later, I want every approved plan to carry all nine sections and every task its own provenance, so that the argument for a change survives the person who made it.
acceptance_criteria: plan save refuses a plan missing any of the nine sections the planner prompt names, or carrying one with an empty body.
A recorded decomposition takes project, story, epic, plan path and plan digest from repository state, and a payload cannot override them.
Task verify_commands must be runnable, required_tests may be empty, and a task dependency may only name an earlier task.
build_waves is no longer authored by the decomposer prompt and its only reader is removed, while the schema still parses artifacts that carry it.
items.outcome: A plan is now refused unless it carries all nine sections the planner prompt mandates, checked with the shared parser instead of a substring that a fenced example could satisfy. A decomposition is bound to the plan it was built from: the recorder stamps project, story, epic, plan_file and the plan digest from trusted state and drops whatever an agent claimed, and stage start refuses when that plan has changed since — or when the binding cannot be verified at all. And build_waves stops being authored anywhere: prompts, the Codex agent contract, the doc and the scaffold check all let go of it together with its only reader, so ordering is derived from dependencies rather than written twice.

items.title: Present the hierarchy to engineers
items.story: As a new engineer, I want the default board screen to tell me what this project is, which stories I can start in parallel right now, and why the others are blocked, so that I can act without opening every card.
acceptance_criteria: Every epic, story and task on screen is explicitly labelled as such, and the drawer opens with a Project > Epic > Story breadcrumb.
/api/state and /api/story/<key> carry project identity, epic membership and derived relationships, and no mutating route exists.
The default view answers what the project is, what can start now, what each epic delivers, and why a story is blocked.
Blocked stories are described as blocked wherever the API reports blocked.
The bundled example passes the production validators and reads correctly at desktop, tablet and mobile widths.
items.outcome: Developers open the board and see the whole project: what it is, which stories can start right now and in how many worktrees, what each epic delivers, and why every blocked story is blocked — with epics, stories and tasks labelled as such and a Project > Epic > Story breadcrumb in the drawer. Blocked now reads as blocked on every surface instead of being folded into 'waiting', and a bundled example project ships that the production capture gates validate, so the board can be seen working before a repo has any work of its own.

items.title: The project knows what it built
items.story: As a developer returning to a project months later, I want the repo itself to tell me everything it has built and where its record begins, so that I can trust what I read instead of reconstructing it from git archaeology.
acceptance_criteria: forge history answers what happened for a story, event type or date range from the committed events, and names events with no story attribution rather than hiding them.
A quickfix window records every product file it touched, including inside an approved story, and the five-file budget still binds where the quickfix is the authorization.
A merged PR is linked to the work it shipped by an event in .factory/events.jsonl, so the link survives a clone with no GitHub remote.
forge init and forge adopt write a boundary marker naming the date, commit and count of preceding commits, and the board reports it instead of implying the record is complete.
Every shipped story has an outcome or an explicit marker that it predates the outcome contract; no outcome is written after the fact for work whose author did not state one.
items.outcome: The repo can now tell you what it built. forge history reads the committed event timeline filtered by story, type, or date and shows events no story owns instead of hiding them. Quickfix windows record every file they touch, so an ad-hoc change is no longer a why with no what. A merged PR is linked to its work by a durable event that survives a clone with no remote — forge pr-link. forge init and adopt stamp an honest 'record begins here' boundary (silent when it cannot be trusted), and forge doctor flags any shipped story with neither an outcome nor a predates-the-contract marker — the two that predate it now carry that marker rather than a fabricated outcome.

items.title: Plan approval is a human gate in plan mode, not an agent command
items.story: As a project owner, I want a plan to reach 'approved' only through my explicit approval in plan mode, so that an agent can never plan, grill, and approve its own work then implement it unchecked.
acceptance_criteria: plan save sets plan_status to awaiting-approval and refuses approved without a fresh .factory/plan-approval.json whose digest matches the plan body, bound to the issue and story.

forge plan approve --by <name> writes the approval marker for the current plan's body digest, issue and story, and is refused without a human --by; it is a human chat confirmation like decision accept.
Implementation stays blocked until plan_status is approved, which now requires the human-attributed marker.
The marker binds the exact plan and context: saving an edited plan, or the same body under a different issue/story, is refused.
Every existing plan-save gate still runs unchanged.
items.outcome: Plan approval is now a human gate an agent cannot forge. forge plan save no longer records a plan as approved on its own — it saves the plan as awaiting-approval and approves only when a fresh approval marker matches that exact plan body under the same issue and story. A human creates that marker with forge plan approve --by "<name>" after reviewing the plan in plan mode, and the marker is consumed on the approved save so it authorizes exactly one save. The result: no product code can be written without a plan a human actually approved, closing the self-approval hole where an agent could plan, grill, and approve its own work. It carries the same trust model as decision accept and client sign-off, with a committed plan-human-approved audit event recording who approved and when.

items.title: Every client-writing command obeys one path-boundary check
items.story: As a developer running forge init, adopt or upgrade against a real project, I want every file the command writes proven to land inside the target before it writes, so that a symlink or symlinked folder can never make it damage a different repository.
acceptance_criteria: init, adopt and upgrade route every write into the target through ONE shared boundary check that refuses a destination resolving outside the target root, including through a symlinked ancestor or .. traversal.
The check runs in preflight, before the first mutation, so an escape stops the command clean rather than mid-write.
Every copytree validates its root destination before the walk and does not follow symlinks into the tree.

Each of the three commands has a per-site test asserting an escape (symlinked destination and symlinked ancestor) is refused; the recurring repository-escape class has a regression test it cannot silently reopen.
A legal in-boundary write behaves exactly as before — the refactor changes safety, not outcomes.
items.outcome: forge init, adopt and upgrade now route every write into the target through one shared, resolved-path boundary check, closing the recurring repository-escape class (decision 0028): a destination or ancestor symlink, a .. traversal, a symlink loop, or a crafted directory that resolves or writes outside the target is refused in a preflight before the first mutation, so an escape aborts clean instead of damaging a different repo. A cross-module structural anti-reopen scan fails the suite if any future raw filesystem write skips the shared helper. Hard-link inode-aliasing and TOCTOU races are documented as a deferred follow-up.

items.title: init and adopt vendor only harness-owned machinery; vendored scaffold-check passes in a client
items.story: As a KnackLabs client running the vendored harness in my repo, I want forge init/adopt to vendor only the harness's own .claude/.codex machinery and the vendored factory-scaffold workflow to run only portable checks, so that my repo's own Claude/Codex skills and private fixtures never make the harness's CI fail.
acceptance_criteria: init and adopt vendor only the harness-owned .claude/.codex manifest (CLAUDE.md, settings.json, skills/forge, codex config, harness agents, codex skills/forge) and never the source repo's other .claude/.codex-skills content
the harness-owned .claude/.codex set is defined once and shared by init, adopt and upgrade, proven by a test
forge init from a source carrying a client .claude/skills/<x>/SKILL.md yields a scaffold without it, and check_dual_runtime is clean
the FORGE-INIT-1 fixture-bound tests skip when their fixture is absent and still run in symphony-forge
init/adopt/upgrade of symphony-forge behave exactly as before (existing tests green)
items.outcome: forge init and adopt now vendor only the harness-owned skill (forge), never a source repo's own skills, so a client repo whose CI runs the vendored factory tests no longer copies a client skill with a canon marker pointing outside the vendored tree into a scaffold — check_dual_runtime stays green in client CI. init/adopt/upgrade share one owned-skill manifest; the three symphony-forge-only fixture tests skip in a fixture-free client scaffold.

items.title: Developer-selectable workflow modes (Lite mode)
items.story: After a PR is raised, small human-supervised fixes shouldn't require the full factory loop. A developer-selectable lite mode gives a bounded, ledgered, one-review lane (terra@high for the delegated fix) that works even post-ship, without loosening the full loop or the trace-only quickfix hatch.
acceptance_criteria: A developer can move a small change through a lighter path than the full loop, chosen deliberately, without hand-editing gate state.
Selecting the lighter path is an attributed, recorded act (who, why) that records which files the change touched.
A change in the lighter path does not ship until it has passed one review with no blocking findings.
A change that exceeds the lighter path's size bound is refused there and directed to the full loop.
The lighter path is available after a story has shipped, not only during it; the full loop and the trace-only hatch are unchanged.
items.outcome: Developers can now make small, human-supervised fixes without the full factory loop. The always-armed planning lock has a third exit: ./forge mode lite --by <name> --reason <why> opens a bounded, ledgered lite window; ./forge fix "<desc>" runs the fix with terra@high (write-enabled); ./forge mode done closes it only after one autoreview pass with no blockers over the committed base_sha..HEAD diff, within the file budget — and this works even post-ship (record_review accepts an open lite window). The full loop and the trace-only quickfix hatch are unchanged.

items.title: Enforcement gates: every PR ties to a complete on-board ticket
items.story: The provenance chain stops one step short of the PR, and board-completeness checks are only advisory, so PRs go untraceable and the board can rot. Add deterministic gates so every PR ties to exactly one complete on-board ticket, the story-PR link is captured automatically on merge, and main stays red until every done story is complete and linked.
acceptance_criteria: A PR cannot merge unless it resolves to exactly one on-board story (or a ledgered mode/quickfix window) whose done-flip and .factory/history/<key>/ archive travel inside the PR's diff (Gate A, a CI required check).
On merge, the story-to-PR link is captured automatically (a merge workflow runs forge pr-link), and the link survives a clone with no remote.
main CI fails if any done story lacks a pr-linked event, an outcome (or predates_outcome_contract), or a .factory/history/<key>/ dir (Gate B, red-main completeness invariant).
Intake refuses a roadmap key that is not on the board, naming the ad-hoc capture path (Gate C).
Every gate is a deterministic script or CI check, not advisory; an agent with no memory of the rules cannot weaken any invariant.
items.outcome: Every PR now ties to a complete on-board ticket, enforced deterministically, so the board can no longer rot silently. Gate C: intake refuses a roadmap key that is not on the board (names the ad-hoc path). Gate A: a required CI check fails any PR that does not resolve to exactly one completed story (its done-flip + .factory/history/<key>/ in the same diff) or a ledgered window. Gate B: a pull_request workflow auto-commits the story-PR link to the branch (no CI writes to main), and check_board_complete verifies every done story has a pr-link + outcome + history. board-invariant ships workflow_dispatch-only; its live push:main enforcement is deferred to D-0011 pending the legacy backfill (the harness's pre-automation done stories).

items.title: JIT task planning: per-task plan+grill against real prior state
items.story: As the harness, I record only the task LIST at decomposition and plan+grill each task's detailed contract just-in-time against the real repo state left by prior tasks, so later tasks stop shipping incorrect code built from speculative upfront contracts.
acceptance_criteria: record_decomposition records the task LIST (id, order, dependencies, one-line objective) but not full per-task contracts; the list is shown under its story on the board from decomposition onward.
A stage's implementation delegation is REFUSED without a fresh, digest-bound per-task grill for that task — the JIT grill is a deterministic gate, exactly as plan save refuses an ungrilled plan.

Each task's detailed contract (write_scope, acceptance, tests, approach) is authored JIT against the actual repo state after prior tasks, and the refinement is recorded as a stage contract change (decision 0023).
A decision record supersedes decision 0007's immutable-upfront-decomposition stance; the shift is deliberate and recorded, not a silent exception.
Both grill points are kept: the story-level plan-grill validates the decomposition; the per-task JIT grill validates each task's details against real prior state.
items.outcome: The factory now records only a task LIST at decomposition and gates each task's detailed contract behind a just-in-time grill: forge delegate <task> refuses a write launch without a fresh, digest-bound passing per-task grill (decision 0032, amending 0007). A task's write_scope/tests/acceptance are authored against what earlier tasks actually built, then grilled, then delegated — so speculative upfront contracts that produce wrong code are gated out. The board renders each task's JIT grill status and a done story's PR link.

items.title: Ad-hoc capture + simplification: one capture path, stories-only board mirror
items.story: As a dev, I capture an ad-hoc 'what about X' with one command as visible spec-debt (no acceptance criteria demanded at capture), and the board mirrors STORIES only, so the epic/story/task/PR mapping is unambiguous and nothing evaporates into chat.
acceptance_criteria: roadmap add --no-spec no longer requires or accepts --ac; the ad-hoc story lands as spec-debt in 'Needs spec', unplannable until spec confirm + link-spec.
WORKFLOW.md 'Source of Truth' mirrors stories only (task state is not mirrored into the tracker), removing the 'are tasks tickets?' ambiguity.
Manual forge pr-link is documented as a degraded-mode fallback only (Gate B's pr-link.yml automates it), not a routine step.
items.outcome: Ad-hoc capture no longer demands acceptance criteria: roadmap add --no-spec --reason works with no --ac, landing the idea as spec-debt that is still unplannable until spec confirm + link-spec (decision 0014 preserved), while --spec stories still require --ac. WORKFLOW.md now mirrors STORIES only (decomposition and task state stay in the repo), removing the are-tasks-tickets ambiguity, and manual forge pr-link is documented as a CI-unavailable fallback since Gate B automates it.

items.title: Project-state audit + legacy pr-link backfill (deterministic core)
items.story: As the harness, I provide a deterministic forge audit that reports every board-completeness and story-shape gap, and I backfill legacy done stories' pr-links from real GitHub merge records (marking genuine gaps, never fabricating), so an upgraded client's board converges to complete and D-0011's red-main invariant can be enabled.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic forge command reports, per repo: done stories missing pr-link/outcome/history; pending stories missing epic/skill/acceptance_criteria/spec; and machinery/vendor drift. Pure over its inputs, CI-runnable, testable.

Legacy done stories get their pr-link recovered from the real GitHub merge record (gh) and recorded via forge pr-link; a genuinely-unrecoverable one is marked predates_outcome_contract. No PR number is fabricated.
The 11 pre-automation done stories are pr-linked or marked so check_board_complete passes, unblocking D-0011 (board-invariant push:main can then be enabled).

Done-story details are reconstructed only from committed evidence (task list from archived decomposition.json, ACs from the archived plan); true evidence-gaps (e.g. never-written outcomes, stub stories) are marked, never synthesized (project-record honesty rule).
items.outcome: Symphony Forge now has a deterministic, contract-driven forge project audit that composes the harness's current validators (so it auto-detects any new requirement as Symphony changes) and rides harness-health.yml's schedule, making project-state drift a continuous check. forge project backfill honestly recovers legacy pr-links from real GitHub merge records (ZERO-match marks predates, TWO+-ambiguous reports, cards reconstructed only from committed evidence, never fabricating). Run on this repo it linked 10 legacy done stories to their real PRs and marked the one evidence-less stub, so check_board_complete passes and board-invariant now enforces on push:main, closing D-0011.

items.title: Safe pending-story repair + backfill provenance honesty
items.story: As the harness, I provide a deterministic forge roadmap fill that repairs an existing pending card by filling only blank fields (refusing active/done cards so shipped history is never overwritten), and I make forge project backfill honest (a zero GitHub match reports unresolved provenance instead of silently marking predates), so the upgrade skill can re-author legacy cards safely.
acceptance_criteria: forge roadmap fill sets ONLY currently-blank fields on a status==pending card and refuses active/done cards (never overwrites shipped history); it records the change.
fill refuses to overwrite a non-blank field (blank-only); a re-run is a safe no-op.

forge project backfill zero-match no longer sets predates_outcome_contract; it reports unresolved provenance and check_board_complete stays red until a human resolves it (pr-link or human-confirmed predates).
A uniquely-recoverable PR still links; the FORGE-BOARD-4 dogfood result stays valid.
items.outcome: Two deterministic primitives close the honesty holes a Codex plan review found. forge roadmap fill safely repairs an existing PENDING card by filling only blank fields and refusing active/done cards, so legacy re-authoring can never overwrite shipped history. forge project backfill no longer auto-marks predates on a zero GitHub match (which could falsely exempt a story whose PR the matcher missed) — it reports unresolved provenance and the board stays red until a human resolves it, with forge project mark-predates the human-confirmed path. Together they make the upgrade skill (FORGE-BOARD-6) able to re-author legacy clients without fabricating history.

items.title: knacklabs-upgrade-project skill (machinery upgrade + guided re-authoring)
items.story: As a dev upgrading an existing client, I run one skill that upgrades the vendored machinery (forge upgrade + doctor --fix), runs the FORGE-BOARD-4 audit, applies the deterministic backfills, and guides me through re-authoring pending stories that are missing details (propose + I confirm) — repeatably, so each run reconverges the board to the current enforced bar.
acceptance_criteria: A knacklabs-upgrade-project skill (the forge-upgrade sibling to knacklabs-migrate-project) orchestrates: machinery upgrade, the audit, deterministic backfills, then guided re-authoring of pending stories (agent proposes ACs/spec/epic, human confirms), and verifies check_vendor_integrity + check_board_complete.
Re-authoring only touches pending/active stories (forward intent), never synthesizes history for done stories; the skill is idempotent and re-runnable.

The skill routes every client-targeting command with --repo TARGET (never the harness), verifies the harness clone's origin/ref/clean before forge upgrade, and frames itself as a periodic convergent runbook (Codex review majors 3/4).
Guided re-authoring uses forge roadmap fill (pending-only, blank-only), never roadmap import on a done card; it never fabricates history.
items.outcome: Symphony Forge now has a knacklabs-upgrade-project operator skill (the forge upgrade sibling to knacklabs-migrate-project) that turns the constant, change-driven upgrade into one runbook: locate the harness robustly, upgrade the machinery, run the project audit + honest backfill, and guide a human through re-authoring only pending stories via forge roadmap fill (never import, never done stories), then re-verify. Every client command routes --repo TARGET so it never touches the harness. It composes the deterministic primitives so the honesty and safety live in the commands, not the prose.

items.title: knacklabs-sanitise-project skill (deterministic repo hygiene)
items.story: As a dev or CI, I run one deterministic sanitise that keeps the client repo canonical (health, roadmap drift, orphaned windows, stale task state, board completeness + PR-links, secrets/cruft), fixing what is mechanically fixable and reporting the rest without ever fabricating, so a vendored client cannot silently rot.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic sanitise (a forge command composing doctor/roadmap heal/project audit + orphaned-window and stale-task-state detection + a cruft scan) fixes what is mechanically fixable and REPORTS the rest; it is runnable on demand and in CI and exits nonzero iff unresolved issues remain.
It never fabricates records (no synthesized outcomes/pr-links); every action is an existing-or-added deterministic command, not a judgement call.

Orphaned mode/quickfix windows and stale task-scoped .factory state (from a crash, not a ship) are detected and REPORTED (clearing stays the human-gated intake --discard-active / mode abandon); board completeness + PR-linkage are verified via forge project audit.
A knacklabs-sanitise-project skill wraps the command as the dev-facing entrypoint, registered in setup (installs to both runtimes).
items.outcome: Symphony Forge gains a one-command repo-hygiene pass, `forge sanitise` (and `--check`): it heals only the safe (roadmap drift, committed cruft) and REPORTS what needs judgment (board gaps, missing PR links, secrets, stale task-state, open windows, advisories) without deleting evidence or fabricating; `--check` is read-only. Three primitives back it: `forge mode abandon` (ledgered close of a crashed window, keeping the harness-marker guard), a pure stale-task-state reporter, and a repo-wide secret/cruft scan. A `knacklabs-sanitise-project` skill wraps it on demand. The daily harness-health cron is gone — the client update check now runs only on `workflow_dispatch` and `push: main` with the cheap version short-circuit, so devs audit on demand and clients stop burning tokens daily.

items.title: Self-updating context ledger
items.story: As a client dev, when I or an agent changes a doc in docs/context/, the ledger updates in the same commit so CI never goes red on a stale ledger
acceptance_criteria: When an agent-session commit follows a docs/context/ change, the ledger updates automatically and its diff rides in the same commit with no manual scan
The git-commit interception re-scans when the commit includes docs/context/ changes (belt for human-made edits)
context scan --check in CI is unchanged and stays green for hook-scanned commits
check_dual_runtime stays green; the seam exists for both runtimes
items.outcome: Editing a context doc no longer reds CI: any git commit through an agent session (either runtime) re-scans docs/context in-process, auto-stages the refreshed ledger.json so the diff rides that same commit, and blocks the commit with the reason while a secret-shaped or oversized context file is unfixed. The write-time hook is deferred with a recorded trigger (D-0015); decision 0035 captures the belt contract.

items.title: Emptiness and coverage are audit failures
items.story: As an operator, a repo with discovery material but no roadmap, no epics, or unreferenced confirmed specs fails project audit and sanitise --check with a named gap instead of reporting OK
acceptance_criteria: project_gaps gains a no-roadmap gap kind: discovery material exists but plans/roadmap.json is absent, empty, or has no epics; project audit and sanitise --check exit non-zero on it
project_gaps gains a spec-coverage gap kind: a confirmed spec no roadmap story references, checked continuously, not only at sign-off
forge doctor reports the missing-roadmap state instead of early-returning clean
The migrate skill gains an explicit post-harvest step naming missing specs/epics/roadmap with the authoring commands; forge adopt's closing hint names specs and roadmap; nothing is auto-generated
items.outcome: Emptiness and coverage are now audit failures, not silence: a repo with discovery material (harvested context, decisions, or confirmed specs) but no roadmap, no stories, or no epics fails forge project audit and sanitise --check with a named no-roadmap gap citing the authoring commands; a confirmed spec no story references is a continuous spec-coverage gap, not a one-time sign-off check; doctor reports the absent-roadmap state; migration (step 7c) and adoption now name capability gaps instead of staying silent - never fabricating content.

items.title: Vendored client gates: roadmap-gate.yml
items.story: As a client team, our PRs cannot land work without declaring a completed story or ledgered window, and our main cannot silently carry coverage gaps - the same teeth the harness has
acceptance_criteria: roadmap-gate.yml joins COPY_WORKFLOWS with a PR job enforcing strict declare-all (client Gate A, decision 0033 contract, no docs-only exemption) and a push-to-main job failing on coverage gaps
Both jobs arm only when plans/roadmap.json exists with at least one epic; an unprepared client does not go red by pulling the upgrade
The arming choice is recorded as a decision record
The vendored-docs client-safety test (0034) still passes with the new workflow vendored
items.outcome: Clients now have the same CI teeth as the harness: the vendored roadmap-gate.yml blocks any PR that lands work without declaring its completed story or ledgered window, and runs the full project audit on every push to the default branch - but only once the client has opted in by authoring a roadmap with at least one epic (decision 0036); unprepared repos and the harness itself stay green. Two Gate A day-one defects fixed at the root: a client's first roadmap PR no longer crashes on the missing base-ref file, and Git Flow feature/<key> branches infer their ticket.

items.title: Terse CLI success paths + budget test
items.story: As an operator, a successful forge command tells me in one line what changed, so the output I do read is the output that matters
acceptance_criteria: Success paths of the chatty commands (stage start/done, plan save/approve, decision new/accept, quickfix start/done, the recorders) print one result line each
Error and refusal messages are unchanged (byte-identical where feasible); forge next keeps full coaching
A budget gate test pins the success-path line counts so lecture-creep cannot return
No new flags, env vars, or config for verbosity
items.outcome: Forge output is terse by default: every touched command's success is one line (state change + identifiers), coaching consolidated into forge next as state-triggered steps that appear only when actionable (commit-the-evidence, commit-the-pin, decision hygiene, spec debt), errors and refusals untouched at full fix-it verbosity, and a budget gate test pins the line counts so lectures cannot creep back. Operators read what matters again.

items.title: Narration budget in the constitution + prompt pointers
items.story: As an operator, agents report state changes and findings, not process commentary, so mid-execution output stays readable
acceptance_criteria: The agent-conduct constitution doc carries the narration budget: one line per state change; findings, contradictions, and gate results always reported; process narration dropped
Full prose stays at gates and deliverables (plans, reviews, PR bodies) per the spec boundary
Phase prompts under factory/prompts/ reference the rule instead of restating it
The rule ships in the vendored canon like the rest of the constitution
items.outcome: The narration budget is contract, not preference: conduct §8 carries the full rule (one line per state change; findings, contradictions, refusals, and gate results never rationed; full prose only at gates and deliverables), AGENTS.md pins it as a strict non-negotiable at exactly the 110-line cap, and the implementer/planner/harvester prompts carry self-sufficient clauses so every delegated worker's brief includes it. Constitution and prompts reach all clients on forge upgrade; the AGENTS.md bullet reaches new clients at init, and existing pilots get it by hand. Enforcement is instruction+review like the rest of the conduct canon - the deterministic half of this epic is TERSE-1's budget test.

items.title: Write lockout + degraded window + routing docs
items.story: As the operator, Claude physically cannot change product or canon - every such change lands through a delegated Codex run or an explicitly ledgered degraded-mode window - so the role split holds by gate, not discipline
acceptance_criteria: With an approved plan and active stage, a session Edit/Write/Bash-write to a product or canon path is denied, naming forge delegate and the degraded-mode window
The same edit inside an open, ledgered degraded-mode window is allowed; the window record rides the PR and Gate A declares it
Orchestration surfaces (docs/specs, decisions, product, memory, context, plans, .factory recorders, git ops on worker diffs) stay writable exactly as today
Adapter and AGENTS.md state the routing within the 110-line cap; docs/degraded-mode.md documents the window; a decision record captures the boundary set
Gate tests pin deny-under-approved-plan, allow-in-window, exemptions, and the window ledger
items.outcome: The role split is now a gate: the orchestrating session physically cannot write product or canon - even under an approved plan - with forge delegate as the sole write path, a ledgered five-file degraded window as the single reasoned exception, and quickfix/lite surviving as work-record tickets (0037 amends 0013/0031, human-confirmed). Read-only Codex rescue works ANYTIME - no stage, no plan, any phase - via a quote-aware guard that also catches env-var laundering. Verified live against its own author: the lockout denied the orchestrator mid-story.

items.title: Zero-setup Windows support: the fail-open core
items.story: As a Windows dev on a new or existing client repo, I get a working harness (hooks, write lock, delegate) without performing any setup myself, so sessions never degrade to hand-typed commands
acceptance_criteria: Hook commands in both runtime configs resolve their interpreter through one shared point (py -3 -> python3 -> python) working on macOS/Linux/Windows Git Bash, failing CLOSED (exit 2) when unresolvable within a working shell
forge.cmd lets cmd/PowerShell users run forge with zero setup; the sh entrypoint is byte-identical for POSIX
forge doctor executes every registered hook command with a benign payload and reports a named RED check per hook that cannot run; forge next on a hook-broken clone names doctor as its first step
A windows-latest harness-internal CI job runs the lockout gate tests and doctor hook-health green; POSIX-only skips are enumerated, not silent
items.outcome: Windows machines are first-class harness hosts with zero user setup: every registered hook resolves through the forge launcher and BLOCKS (exit 2) instead of silently disarming when anything in its chain is missing; cmd/PowerShell users get a native forge.cmd that only trusts real executables (an argument-injection class was found and eliminated in review); doctor executes all eight registered hook commands verbatim and names exactly what is broken; recorders and the delegation lock work on Windows (lazy fcntl, msvcrt); CRLF and cp1252 encodings can no longer corrupt the launcher or crash output; and a windows-latest CI job now proves the armed lockout path on every PR. New clients get all of it at init; existing clients on their next forge upgrade.

items.title: Read-only rescue accepts long prompts via prompt-file
items.story: As the orchestrator, a long read-only exploration brief reaches Codex through a file-based prompt, so the anytime contract holds beyond short inline prompts
acceptance_criteria: The companion guard allowlists --prompt-file for read-only task invocations (file content is data, not argv)
The rescue route works with a multi-paragraph brief, live-verified
items.outcome: Long read-only exploration briefs now reach Codex: the companion guard admits task --prompt-file with a repo-contained regular file (resolved-both-sides containment; absolute, traversal, escaping-symlink, dangling, directory, duplicate, wrong-verb, and equals shapes all still refused), so the anytime rescue contract holds beyond short inline prompts — live-verified with a multi-paragraph brief in both directions. Write delegation and every other guard refusal are unchanged.

items.title: Doctor --fix installs prerequisites on Windows
items.story: As a Windows dev with no Git or Python, forge doctor --fix converges the machine to green with no user-typed setup and at most one consolidated elevation confirm
acceptance_criteria: On Windows missing Git or Python, doctor --fix converges to green with no user-typed setup and at most one UAC confirm
init/adopt/upgrade each leave a client repo hook-healthy on Windows; upgrade replaces pinned-interpreter settings
items.outcome: A Windows machine with no Git or Python converges to a working harness by running 'forge doctor --fix' with zero typed setup: it adds a real Python 3.10+ check, installs Git and Python in user scope via winget, finds them through canonical known folders plus ProgramW6432 (WOW64-safe), and refreshes PATH so the fixing run reports green — or prints honest guidance when it cannot. forge.cmd lets cmd/PowerShell users run the harness natively and bootstraps Python before the Git Bash handoff. Auto-remediation refuses to run under an elevated shell (fail-closed), never executing user-writable installers as admin. New clients get it at init, existing on forge upgrade, and windows-latest CI proves it. The single-UAC elevation batch is deferred to real-Windows validation (D-0021).

items.title: Delegation runs on native Windows
items.story: As a Windows dev, forge delegate launches and supervises Codex workers without POSIX-only process machinery, so implementation works end to end
acceptance_criteria: delegate.py replaces fcntl/ps/killpg/preexec_fn with cross-platform equivalents; a delegation completes on windows-latest CI
The recorded delegate invocation shows injected sandbox flags (unelevated, workspace-write) on Windows
items.outcome: Symphony Forge delegations now run end-to-end on native Windows: forge delegate launches, supervises, and reaps Codex workers through a single psutil-based process model (decision 0042) on both Windows and POSIX — retiring the ps/killpg machinery and its lstart fragility. psutil ships as the harness's first runtime Python dependency, gated by a required doctor row and installed by doctor --fix (venv-aware, PEP-668-honest, converges in one run). Windows workers record the workspace-write sandbox; the unelevated tightening stays deferred (D-0021). The windows-hook-gates CI selector gains a real Windows launch/reap E2E.

items.title: Workers run sandboxed by default
items.story: As an operator, delegated workers run workspace-write sandboxed in every client instead of danger-full-access, verified against a real delegation
acceptance_criteria: Vendored .codex/config.toml defaults to workspace-write; a real delegation passes end to end under it; the escape hatch for genuinely-broader tasks is documented and ledgered
check_vendor_integrity hashes .codex/hooks.json; a decision record covers the default flip
items.outcome: Every vendored Codex session in every client now defaults to workspace-write instead of full machine access, and the fail-closed hook wiring (.codex/hooks.json) is frozen vendor surface — a client edit that disarms a hook fails check_vendor_integrity by name at pr-ready. Broader access remains possible only as a deliberate, diff-visible config edit that forge upgrade reverts (decision 0041). Delegated workers were already workspace-write via the companion; the flip closes the dormant default, and the story's own delegation proved the boundary live when the sandbox refused the worker's .codex write.

items.title: Review verifies plan contracts
items.story: As an orchestrator, I want review to verdict every plan contract so that incomplete implementation blocks pr-ready instead of passing invisibly.
acceptance_criteria: Decomposition tasks may declare validated plan_contracts
forge review-brief composes per-task and --all contract briefs
Quality review artifact must verdict every declared contract; partial/missing is a blocking finding
pr_ready refuses until all declared contracts are verified implemented
Tasks without plan_contracts behave exactly as today
items.outcome: Review is no longer plan-blind: decomposition tasks can declare plan_contracts (the plan invariants they must satisfy), ./forge review-brief composes the reviewer's contract prompt (per-task or --all for the branch-wide closeout), the quality review artifact must verdict every declared contract with evidence — partial or missing verdicts become blocking findings — and pr-ready refuses until every contract is verified implemented. Incomplete implementation now blocks the gate instead of passing invisibly; tasks without contracts behave exactly as before.

items.title: No code page can break the harness (encoding hardening)
items.story: As a Windows developer on a default cp1252 console, I can run every forge flow — doctor, verify, delegation, evidence recording — without an encoding crash or mojibake, so that the zero-setup promise holds on machines we never configured.
acceptance_criteria: One shared decode convention for captured child output: common.run_quiet, stages' required-test/verify runners, and delegate's capture points decode utf-8 with errors=replace via a single helper (run_cmd landed in PR #101); no call-site drift remains (audited).

Text file I/O in factory/scripts is explicit: every read_text/write_text/open of a text file names encoding=utf-8 (plan/spec readers, delegate worker logs, evidence writers); a structural check or test refuses new locale-default text I/O.

windows-latest CI proves the flows under a FORCED cp1252 console (PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252 or chcp 1252): forge next, doctor, a delegation launch, and verify all exit clean — the regression net GH's utf-8-friendly default never provides.
Vendored clients receive the hardening: the existing init/adopt/upgrade propagation tests cover the touched scripts.

items.title: JIT frontier is enforced, not advisory
items.story: As an orchestrator, I want stage start and forge next to refuse or route around an unauthored or ungrilled frontier task so that no implementation begins before its contract exists and survived an independent grill
acceptance_criteria: record_decomposition_from_json.py refuses execution detail (write_scope, required_tests, verify_commands) on any task after the earliest pending leaf and accepts it on the frontier task

a shared require_ready_task() makes stage start and delegate both refuse an incomplete contract or missing/stale grill; an active stage with empty write_scope refuses instead of silently degrading to read-only; explicit --read-only still passes
forge next reports author-contract / grill / stage-start / delegate as the single next action per task state
docs/FACTORY.md, WORKFLOW.md, and factory/prompts/decomposer.md state the enforced JIT contract with no upfront-contract contradiction
items.outcome: Implementation can no longer begin before its contract exists and survived an independent grill: the decomposition recorder refuses execution detail on future tasks, a shared readiness gate makes stage start and delegate refuse incomplete or ungrilled frontier contracts (and the silent empty-scope read-only downgrade is gone), and forge next walks the dev through the JIT loop one action at a time - enter plan mode and author, grill, start, delegate. The docs now say what the gates enforce. A dev following the rail cannot skip contract authoring or grilling by accident.

items.title: Grills carry proof, diffs stay reviewable
items.story: As an orchestrator, I want task grills to require repository-grounded proofs bound to an internally derived digest, and stage done to refuse over-budget diffs, so that empty rubber-stamp grills and unreviewable changes stop being representable
acceptance_criteria: a task grill missing inspected_refs (existing paths), current_flow, a total criteria_map, a keep/split/block decision, or the declare-or-empty new_abstractions field is refused; pass with split/block refused; block without an escalation packet refused

the recorder derives the grill digest from the full task contract, the approved-plan digest excluding appended assumptions, and a product-tree hash excluding .factory/ and plans/; caller-supplied --task-digest is removed; contract, plan, and product-tree changes stale the grill while .factory/ and plans/ commits do not
the frontier task's criteria_map lands as plan_contracts so the existing FORGE-REV-2 quality review verdicts each criterion

stage done refuses a diff over the task's review budget (default 8 files / 400 lines excluding .factory/ and plans/; lower free, higher needs a written reason) and the composed brief states the budget
the board renders the in-flight story's task rows (state, grill freshness, budget usage) from the same derivation forge next uses
items.outcome: A task can no longer be implemented on an unproven plan: its grill must show what was inspected, how the system currently flows, how every acceptance criterion will be proven, what new abstractions are justified, and which resolutions the operator personally chose (recorded question-options-chosen rounds) or a document dictated (named citations) - and the recorder derives the binding itself from the contract, the approved plan, and the product tree, so nothing self-asserted survives an edit. Diffs stay reviewable: stage done refuses more than 8 files/400 lines unless a written reason raised it, the task graph is frozen except for skeletal appends (so splits work), completed contracts are immutable, and the board now shows every task's state, grill freshness, and budget live.

items.title: Approval and closeout integrity
items.story: As an orchestrator, I want plan approval, per-stage review, commits, branch review, and closeout artifacts bound and ordered by deterministic gates so that an edited plan, an unreviewed commit, an incoherent review, or an out-of-order artifact cannot reach pr_ready
acceptance_criteria: approved plan save stores approved_plan_sha256 (excluding the assumptions appendix); implementation gates rederive it; plan approve refuses without a fresh matching plan grill on an awaiting plan; an edited plan requires re-grill and re-approval

the task grill records approved_by stamped from the operator's sanctioned rounds AFTER the grill passes; require_ready_task refuses a grill without the approval stamp, bound to the same grounding digest, so an approved-then-edited contract needs re-grill and re-approval

forge next planning routes a pre-draft requirements round: before the story plan is drafted, the confirmed spec is re-grilled against current repository state with rounds via AskUserQuestion, and drafting is instructed only after that pass records

initial decomposition recording refuses execution detail (including reviewer_focus and plan_contracts) on every task; later recordings freeze the initial id/order/dependency skeleton; completed task contracts are immutable under a full-contract digest

a clean local-review stamp bound to stage id, task digest, brief SHA, baseline, and pre-commit diff digest is recorded in stages.json; stage done refuses a missing/stale stamp, uncommitted or staged product changes, or an empty committed stage delta
the three review lenses carry one review_run_id bound to a fresh review-brief --all SHA and the branch diff digest; incoherent lens sets are refused

closeout is ordered by gates: all stages done, then branch review, then verify, then functional when user_facing, then outcome, then pr_ready; pr_ready additionally requires a clean product worktree/index, repo-kind-aware evidence exclusions, and the outcome stamp on the same commit
opening a lite, quickfix, or degraded write window while a stage is active refuses
items.outcome: Approval and closeout integrity is enforced end to end: an edited plan, an unreviewed commit, an out-of-order or unstamped artifact, or a mid-stage write window can no longer reach pr_ready. Plans bind by digest and need a fresh human-attributed grill+approval; every task is grilled, planned, and approved before implementation; the confirmed spec is re-grilled against repo reality before drafting; each stage closes only with a clean local-review stamp over its committed delta; the three lenses are one coherent run; closeout is ordered on a clean tree with the outcome on the evidence commit; no window opens mid-stage. Also builds decision 0047 task-level shipping (task start/pr-ready, marker-on-main, marker-aware frontier, CI task markers), bootstrapped story-level.

items.title: Story state stops conflicting across PRs
items.story: As an orchestrator running parallel story worktrees, I want all recorded story evidence scoped per story with no archive move, no shared append ledger, and a merge-survivable hook, so that overlapping PRs merge without .factory conflicts and a conflicted tree can always be repaired through sanctioned commands
acceptance_criteria: two story worktrees recording concurrently produce zero overlapping .factory paths and a merge simulation in the gate tests yields no .factory conflicts
pr_ready ships in place with no archive move; shipped evidence stays at its recorded story-scoped paths and forge history and the board read it
events are one file each (0022 pattern); forge history reads legacy events.jsonl and per-event files together; no merge-driver dependency remains
the active-story pointer is worktree-local; phase derives from story artifacts; no tracked run.json authority remains
forge next auto-heals the roadmap after a merge commit

with unmerged index entries the hook permits git-native resolution of exactly those paths and refuses content hand-writes; an unparseable factory_lib or state file engages a static deny-list fallback instead of crashing
items.outcome: Overlapping story PRs no longer conflict on .factory state. Story evidence is story-scoped (.factory/stories/<KEY>/), the active-story run pointer is worktree-local and untracked with phase derived from artifacts, events are one conflict-free file each (union merge driver retired), pr_ready ships in place with no archive move, and the PreToolUse/Stop hooks survive a merge — engaging a self-contained deny-list that keeps writes locked but permits git-native recovery instead of crashing, so a conflict-markered run.json or factory_lib can never trap a session again. Intake activates the new layout; legacy repos stay readable and pick it up via forge upgrade. Proven by a two-worktree merge simulation with zero .factory conflicts.

items.title: Pilot: measure the last 20 shipped stories from committed records
items.story: As the harness maintainer, I want a throwaway read-only script to project this repo's committed events, ledgers and PR links for the last ~20 shipped stories and report coverage, join rate and right-first-time agreement, so that we know whether broad instrumentation is worth owning before changing any recorder.
acceptance_criteria: Report committed under docs/memory/ with: % stories with exactly one usable intake and shipped event; join rate to merged PRs; orphan/unmerged event count; duplicate/malformed/event-loss rate; agreement between event-derived and human-labelled right-first-time on 10 sampled stories
Decision export-privacy-boundary drafted with the boundary text from the spec (authority, field rule, titles, consumer-owned identity and collection policy) and presented for human acceptance
No recorder, schema or hook changes; script is not vendored

items.title: Stable event id and strict discriminated event schema
items.story: As a consumer of the ledger, I want every event to carry its id, optional task/signal_id/attempt and a per-kind typed data object that the validator enforces closed, so that records are joinable and can never carry prose.
acceptance_criteria: Every event payload carries id equal to its file name; existing readers (forge history, pr_ready) accept both old and new payloads

Event schema is discriminated per kind with constrained scalar types (nonnegative_number, boolean, sha256, opaque_id, safe_token, closed enums); the validator enforces nested closed objects; a recorder test with an undeclared key or free string in data fails
export-privacy-boundary is accepted (human) before this story's plan is saved

items.title: Read-only exporter over a committed ref
items.story: As cadence (or any local consumer), I want `forge events export --ref <ref>` to write factory-export/v1 NDJSON of event and roadmap records reachable at that ref with a header carrying schema, harness_commit, integrity_status and coverage, so that I can measure factory cycle time and roadmap progress without reading the repo.
acceptance_criteria: factory/schemas/factory-export.json checked in; CI validates the export of this repo at HEAD; running twice yields identical output; --no-titles removes titles; grep for detail, paths, branch names or prose fixtures finds nothing
Header integrity_status comes from the existing vendor-integrity check (clean|drifted|unarmed) and flips to drifted when one vendored gate file is edited; no new manifest
Events are grouped into runs per intake; the run ending in shipped is primary, earlier runs carry run_status abandoned; roadmap records carry epic id, story key, status, dependencies, PR link, titles
Success prints one line; coverage and drift details are findings; forge upgrade carries schema and exporter to a client repo

items.title: Source metrics the views consume
items.story: As a consumer, I want verify duration and check counts, numeric tests run/failed, review blocking/non-blocking counts per lens, signal resolution elapsed seconds and resolver, stage-close measured diff and attempt, and plan-save attempt and result recorded at their sources and projected into event data, so that right-first-time and redo causes are computable.
acceptance_criteria: Artifact schemas (verify, test-automated, review, signal ledger, stages, plans) gain the numeric fields; recorders populate them; each field is consumed by a named metric in the spec
stage-done, verify-*, tests-*, review-*, signal-resolved, plan-saved events carry the declared data keys; gate-test happy path plus review-rework and plan-revision scenarios prove them
right-first-time (attempt == 1 across stage/verify/review/plan-save, no stage-incomplete) is computable from the export of the gate-test fixture

items.title: Missing transitions consumed by named metrics
items.story: As a consumer, I want grill-recorded, plan-saved, outcome-set and decision-accepted to emit events, and quickfix/degraded/lesson/signal ledgers projected by the exporter rather than duplicated, so that the story lifecycle in the export is complete for the metrics the views name.
acceptance_criteria: grill-recorded (gate, rounds, questions_asked, verdict), plan-saved (attempt, result), outcome-set and decision-accepted emitted with declared data; grill records require rounds and questions_asked
Exporter projects quickfix, degraded, lesson and signal ledger records as event records with source ids; no duplicate global events are written
forge history renders the new events; export of the gate-test fixture contains every transition the spec lists

items.title: Ship-cleanup clears .git/forge authority
items.story: As a harness maintainer, I want story ship-cleanup to clear the git-local .git/forge stage authority — and load_stages to ignore it when no story is active — so that a shipped story's stale authority can never phantom-deadlock the next window.
acceptance_criteria: On ship, pr_ready clears .git/forge/{stages,decomposition}.json (and delegations.jsonl, locks/), not only archiving to .factory/history/<KEY>/
load_stages returns {} when the run has no issue_key (no active story), so leftover authority never reports a phantom active stage
Regression test: an orphaned .git/forge/stages.json (no current issue, or issue != current) does not block forge quickfix/mode/stage start
items.spec_debt_reason: hardening follow-up from the 2026-08-19 WIN-2 stale-authority deadlock (see plans/lessons); no confirmed spec yet

items.title: Upgrade preserves and truthfully reports doc-contract overwrites
items.story: As a client running forge upgrade, I want doc-contract files I appended to (e.g. docs/architecture/README.md) preserved to a .orig backup and named in the report — never silently overwritten while the summary calls the directory 'Untouched (project-owned)' — so I cannot lose project content invisibly.
acceptance_criteria: The upgrade report names each replaced doc-contract destination path, and no longer implies a directory whose contract file was overwritten is fully untouched

When a client's doc-contract file differs from the new template, the upgrade names it and warns — pointing the operator at `git diff` (prior content is committed; upgrade requires a clean tree) — so divergence is never reported as 'untouched'; no backup files are created

Regression test: upgrading a client whose doc-contract README differs from the template names it replaced and emits the divergence warning, while an identical unedited file is not warned and no .orig files appear

items.title: Stage-done proof runner: read-only check excludes workflow paths; reap scan scales
items.story: As a developer closing a stage, I want the stage-done proof runner to enforce read-only only on PRODUCT paths and to reap the proof's process tree without a full process-table scan, so a verify_command that writes .factory evidence cannot false-fail the close and a busy machine cannot hang it.
acceptance_criteria: Stage-done's 'proof must be read-only' check compares only product paths (excludes .factory/ and plans/), so a verify_command that appends evidence there does not fail the close
The stage-done reap (_wait_and_reap) does not degrade on a large unrelated process table: the process-tree observation is scoped/bounded, not a full psutil scan polled every 20ms
Regression tests: a verify_command writing under .factory passes the read-only check; the reap completes promptly regardless of unrelated process count
items.spec_debt_reason: hardening follow-up from the 2026-08-20 issue-#112 story where stage done could not close (verify.py in verify_commands tripped the read-only check; reap scan spun on a bloated process table); no confirmed spec yet

items.title: Plan mode and grill provenance are enforced, not advisory
items.story: As the harness owner, I want story plans and task plans to be refused unless they were authored in plan mode and grilled through recorded AskUserQuestion rounds until the frontier was empty, so that the planning discipline is a gate the recorder checks rather than a reminder the session can skip.
acceptance_criteria: A PostToolUse hook on ExitPlanMode records a story-scoped marker (timestamp, sha256 of the plan text); plan save and task plan save refuse a --from file whose digest has no marker in the active story window

A PostToolUse hook logs every AskUserQuestion (question texts) into a story-scoped ledger; the grill recorder for spec, requirements, plan and task gates requires each rounds[].question to match a logged question and enforces a per-gate minimum of rounds or an explicit frontier-empty attestation on the final round
Recorders refuse a task grill recorded before the task plan is saved; forge next prints the enforced order: plan mode -> grill rounds -> save -> human approval
Gate tests cover: plan authored outside plan mode is refused; grill with unlogged rounds is refused; the happy path passes; vendored to clients by forge upgrade
items.outcome: Plan-mode and grill discipline are now gates the recorders enforce, not reminders. A PostToolUse hook records who authored every plan (plan-mode markers) and every question actually put to a human (AskUserQuestion rounds with chosen answers); plan and task-plan save/approve refuse a plan without a matching marker, and spec, requirements, plan and task grills refuse rounds not in the ledger, below the per-gate floor, or missing the frontier-empty attestation. The task loop runs plan, then grill, then human approval, then stage start — printed by forge next and pinned by tests. A session can no longer save a plan authored outside plan mode or record a grill that never asked a human anything; the story proved it on itself, its own gates refusing its own plan and grill until done right.

epics.title: Symphony Forge
epics.objective: Turn in-repo architecture and decisions into shipped applications through a deterministic software-factory workflow.

epics.title: Traceable board: complete, JIT-planned, backtrackable
epics.objective: Make the epic/story/task/PR/ticket board complete and PR-linked, enforced deterministically so it cannot rot and agents can always backtrack; plan each task just-in-time against real prior state; and give clients skills to upgrade and sanitise into this bar.

epics.title: The record updates itself, and clients are held to the roadmap
epics.objective: Ledgers auto-update on doc changes, emptiness/coverage gaps are audit failures, and vendored CI gates hold every client to the declare-all roadmap contract

epics.title: Terse by default: output earns its lines
epics.objective: One-line command successes, coaching only in forge next and errors, a vendored narration budget for agents; reading load drops without losing the durable record

epics.title: The role split is a gate: only Codex writes product
epics.objective: Session writes to product and canon are hook-denied even under an approved plan; forge delegate is the sole write path; discovery routes to Codex rescue; a ledgered degraded-mode window is the only exception

epics.title: Windows is a first-class host: the harness self-heals, no user setup
epics.objective: Make the harness work on Windows for new and existing clients with zero user-performed setup: portable fail-closed hooks, doctor auto-remediation, delegate-time Codex config, forge-next self-heal trigger, and windows-latest CI.

epics.title: Review is plan-aware: contracts get verdicts
epics.objective: Bind review to the plan: tasks declare plan contracts, review verdicts each one with evidence, and pr-ready refuses until every contract is verified implemented.

epics.title: Accountable engineering loop
